description:
draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §5.11 (line 2010 onward) defines two extra arguments on CalendarEvent/query:
- expandRecurrences: Boolean (default false) — when true, the server expands recurring events into one synthetic id per occurrence within the [after, before] window
- timeZone: TimeZoneId (default 'Etc/UTC') — for evaluating the before/after filter conditions

§5.11 also defines two new method-level errors:
- expandDurationTooLarge: when expandRecurrences:true and (before-after) > maxExpandedQueryDuration
- cannotCalculateOccurrences: when the backend cannot expand a recurrence required to satisfy the query

src/event.rs:569-574 (handle_calendar_event_query) just delegates to jmap_server::handlers::handle_query::<CalendarEvent, B>. The generic /query handler has no concept of expandRecurrences. The args are forwarded as-is to the QueryObject filter machinery, which has no plumbing for these JSCalendar-specific concepts. Result: expandRecurrences:true is silently ignored, and the new error codes can never be produced from this handler.

PLAN.md §8 explicitly described this contract — the backend produces the synthetic ids and the handler maps cannotCalculateOccurrences from a backend error. Neither piece exists.

Same gap applies to handle_calendar_event_query_changes (no extra arg handling) but that method does not have these extra args in the spec, so /queryChanges is correct as-is.

Wire impact: clients using expandRecurrences (the documented way to get per-occurrence ids for /get) silently receive only the master event id and have to parse recurrenceRule themselves — an entire feature is missing.

Test gap: no inline test exercises expandRecurrences. The 'registers_all_20_methods' test sends filter:null and never tests this code path.

Fix: define a CalendarEventQueryArgs struct, add a parse step in handle_calendar_event_query, add a query_calendar_events method (or accept_args param) on CalendarsBackend, and map backend errors to expandDurationTooLarge / cannotCalculateOccurrences method errors via JmapError::custom or a new JmapError constructor in jmap-types.
title: CalendarEvent/query §5.11 expandRecurrences/timeZone unimplemented; expandDurationTooLarge/cannotCalculateOccurrences not produced
